assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Gamete
items.clue: A haploid sex cell produced by meiosis.

items.label: Standard deviation
items.clue: A statistic that describes the spread of a set of repeat measurements around their mean.

items.label: Isotonic solution
items.clue: A solution that has the same solute concentration as the solution it is being compared with.

items.label: Hypotonic solution
items.clue: A solution that has a lower solute concentration than the solution it is being compared with, such as the cytoplasm of a cell.

questions.stem: Red blood cells are placed in distilled water. What happens to them, and why?

options.text: Water enters by osmosis and the cells swell until their membranes are stretched taut, and then they remain turgid.
Water leaves by osmosis, because the cytoplasm is more concentrated than the distilled water, and the cells shrink.
Water leaves by osmosis, because distilled water is hypertonic to the cytoplasm, and the cells crenate.
Water enters by osmosis and the cells swell and burst, because no wall resists their expansion.

questions.stem: A plant cell is placed in pure water. What happens to it?

options.text: Water enters by osmosis and the cell swells until it bursts, like an animal cell in pure water.
Solutes leave the cell into the pure water until the cell sap is as dilute as the water outside.
The cell pumps water in, using energy, until it is full and then it switches the pumping off.
Water enters by osmosis and the cell becomes turgid, its wall resisting further expansion.

questions.stem: What is the relative advantage of sexual reproduction over asexual reproduction?

options.text: Its offspring carry new gene combinations, giving the variation needed for a changed environment.
Its offspring gain the particular features that a changed environment comes to require.
Its offspring are better adapted than the parent in every environment, so more of them survive.
Its offspring carry new alleles produced by meiosis, which asexual offspring cannot receive.

questions.stem: A student annotates a diagram of the male reproductive system. Which annotation is correct?

options.text: Urethra: carries urine only, because semen leaves through a separate duct in the penis.
Epididymis: stores sperm while they mature after their production in the testis.
Seminal vesicle: stores the sperm until they are required for ejaculation.
Testis: produces the semen that carries sperm along the duct to the urethra.

questions.explanation: Sperm are produced in the testis and pass into the epididymis, the coiled tube on its surface, where they mature and are stored until ejaculation.

questions.stem: Which statement about the tissue fluid that bathes the cells of a mammal is correct?

options.text: It is kept slightly hypotonic to the cytoplasm of the cells, so that they are kept fully hydrated by a steady inflow of water.
It is kept isotonic with the cytoplasm of the cells, so that they neither swell and burst nor shrink through net osmosis.
It is kept isotonic with the cytoplasm of the cells, so that no water molecules cross their membranes at all.
Its concentration does not need regulating, because cells that take in excess water become turgid and then stop.

questions.stem: A student annotates a diagram of the female reproductive system. Which annotation is correct?

options.text: Uterus: the site of fertilization and, later, of implantation of the embryo.
Endometrium: the thick muscular wall of the uterus that contracts during childbirth.
Oviduct: the site of fertilization; it moves the egg towards the uterus.
Ovary: releases an egg into the oviduct on day 1 of each menstruation.

questions.explanation: The oviduct collects the egg released at ovulation, its cilia move the egg towards the uterus, and it is where sperm normally meet and fertilize the egg.

questions.stem: In humans, a gene codes for the enzyme tyrosinase, which catalyses a step in the synthesis of the pigment melanin. A person with two non-functional alleles of this gene has albinism. What is the direct product of expressing this gene?

options.text: The pigment melanin, which the gene codes for
The enzyme tyrosinase, made by translation
The skin colour that the gene determines
More copies of the gene in each skin cell

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the promoter of a gene in a eukaryotic cell?

options.text: The first part of the gene to be transcribed, which codes for the first amino acids of the polypeptide
A protein that binds to an enhancer sequence and increases the rate of transcription of the gene
A sequence near the start of the gene to which transcription factors and RNA polymerase bind
A base sequence that RNA polymerase binds to by itself, with no other proteins required

questions.stem: A liver cell and a neuron from the same person are compared. Which comparison is correct?

options.text: They have different genomes, because each has kept different genes
They have the same transcriptome, because both cells transcribe all of their genes
They have the same genome but different transcriptomes and proteomes
They have the same proteome, because the same genes code for the same proteins

questions.explanation: The genome is the same in all body cells. The two cells express different sets of genes, so the RNA present (transcriptome) and the proteins present (proteome) differ, and this is what makes them differentiated.

questions.stem: Cytosine bases in the DNA of a gene's promoter become methylated. What is the effect on the gene?

options.text: Transcription of the gene downstream is repressed, so it is not expressed
Translation of the gene's mRNA is blocked, because ribosomes cannot read methylated codons
The base sequence of the gene is altered, so a different polypeptide is produced from it
Transcription of the gene is increased, because the methyl tag marks it for expression

questions.stem: In a skin cell, the promoter of gene G is methylated and the gene is not expressed. The cell divides by mitosis. What is the most likely state of gene G in the daughter cells, and why?

options.text: Expressed, because epigenetic tags are lost whenever DNA is replicated
Not expressed, because the methylation has changed the base sequence of the gene
Not expressed, because the methyl tags remained in place through mitosis
Not expressed in the person's children, because the tags pass to offspring

questions.stem: Why is it important that most epigenetic tags are removed from the DNA of the sperm and the ovum?

options.text: So that no epigenetic tag from either parent is able to affect the offspring's cells
So that the cells of the embryo can develop a fresh pattern of differentiation
So that the base sequence of the offspring's DNA is restored to normal
So that every gene in the zygote is switched off until it is needed

questions.explanation: Removing most of the tags from the gametes means the embryo is not committed to the expression patterns of the parents' cells, so its cells can differentiate into every cell type. The tags that are not removed are the exception that makes ligers and tigons differ.
